Respiratory Chain Defects
Th e respiratory chain (see Figure 26.5) is made up of ﬁ ve com-
plexes that undergo changes in their oxidative state to produce
ATP (adenosine triphosphate). Carbohydrates are eventually 
metabolized to pyruvate, which will then enter into the Krebs 
cycle. Electrons generated from the Krebs cycle and from beta-
oxidation of fatty acids are used in the production of energy via 
the complexes of the respiratory chain. Defects aﬀ ecting several 
of the individual complexes have been identiﬁ ed. Th ese defects
lead to decreased energy production in various tissues, and
